title: Savitch’s space inclusion
statement: Let $S\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\log_2 n+1\le S(n)$ for every $n$, and suppose that for some positive integer $c$ there is a finite deterministic Turing machine that, on every binary input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $S(|x|)$ using at most $cS(|x|)$ work-tape cells. Then every language decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of $S(n)$ work-tape cells is decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine using at most a constant multiple of $S(n)^2$ work-tape cells.
